claim.claim-text: 1. An apparatus for determining a depth of a burn wound, said apparatus comprising:

a plurality of electrodes capable of forming one or more capacitive sensors configured to measure a capacitance of a region of tissue proximate to each said capacitive sensor, a drive circuit electronically coupled to each said capacitive sensor, a processor electronically coupled to said drive circuit, and a non-transitory computer-readable medium electronically coupled to said processor and comprising instructions stored thereon that, when executed on said processor, perform the steps of:

receiving information regarding said measured capacitance from said capacitive sensor via said drive circuit, comparing said information to a data array comprising pairs of capacitances and depths of burns, and determining the depth of said burn wound associated with said measured capacitance.

said step of receiving information regarding said measured capacitance comprises: receiving a first capacitance measured at a first location of known unaffected tissue, receiving a second capacitance measured at a second location within said burn wound, and determining a capacitance difference between said first and second capacitances;
3. The apparatus of claim 1 or 2, wherein:

said instructions further comprise the step of converting each measured capacitance to an associated sub-epidermal moisture (SEM) value, said data array comprises pairs of SEM values and depths of burns, said step of comparing said information to said data array comprises comparing said SEM value to said data array, and said step of determining the depth of said burn wound comprises identifying the depth of said burn wound associated with said SEM value.
4. The apparatus of any one of claims 1-3, wherein said one or more capacitive sensors are virtual capacitive sensors, comprising more than two electrodes of said plurality of electrodes.
5. The apparatus of claim 4, wherein each of said virtual capacitive sensors comprises a virtual center electrode and a virtual ring electrode.

6. The apparatus of claim 5, wherein said drive circuit is configured to select one or more electrodes of said plurality of electrodes to form said virtual center electrode, and select more than two or more electrodes of said plurality of electrodes to form said virtual ring electrodes.
7. The apparatus of claim 5 or 6, further comprising a gap between said virtual center electrode and virtual ring electrode.
8. The apparatus of claim 7, wherein said drive circuit is further configured to measure said capacitance between said virtual center electrode and virtual ring electrode.
9. The apparatus of claim 7, wherein the gap between said virtual center electrode and said virtual ring electrode is varied to change a characteristic of an electric field.
10. The apparatus of claim 9, wherein said characteristic of an electric field comprises depth of said electric field.
11. The apparatus of claim 7, wherein said gap is uniform.
12. The apparatus of claim 7, wherein said gap is variable.
13. The apparatus of any one of claims 1-3, wherein a subset of said plurality of electrodes are connected to a common element of a circuit to form a virtual sensor.
14. The apparatus of any one of claims 1-3, wherein each said capacitive sensor consists of a pair of electrodes of said plurality of electrodes.
